## What it is

Gelman named this after the legal scholar whose government memos damaged his academic standing. The idea is that a scholar's reputation is an asset that makes careful work worth doing: people listen, so accuracy pays. Once the reputation is gone, so that nothing you write will be taken seriously, the incentive to be careful disappears. Past that point you "might as well become a hack," writing for whichever audience still rewards you.

## Why it matters

The concept explains why some public intellectuals seem to get *worse* after a credibility crisis instead of trying to rebuild. The incentives have flipped. It also warns readers that once a source has crossed the line, the usual assumption that a credentialed expert is trying to be accurate no longer holds.

## How it works

Model the audience's belief that the author is *reliable* rather than a *hack* as a posterior probability, updated after each piece of work by whether it held up. Above the line, readers pay attention and every piece counts. Below it, they mostly stop reading, so careful new work is rarely even noticed and trust cannot rebuild. The return to carefulness collapses, which is the line. This is a toy model of the incentive, not a claim about any particular person.

## Simulated example

An author publishes 60 pieces. Each piece is accurate with probability equal to their care level, which drops partway through. The audience updates its trust only when it is paying attention. Watch trust cross the line and see how slowly it recovers once care returns.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import {rng, range} from "../js/stats.js"
```

```{ojs}
viewof lapseStart = Inputs.range([5, 40], {value: 15, step: 1, label: "When the author gets careless (piece #)"})
viewof lapseLength = Inputs.range([0, 30], {value: 12, step: 1, label: "How long the lapse lasts"})
viewof line = Inputs.range([0.2, 0.8], {value: 0.5, step: 0.05, label: "Trust threshold (the line)"})
viewof seed = Inputs.range([1, 500], {value: 41, step: 1, label: "Random seed"})
```

```{ojs}
trust = {
  const r = rng(seed);
  // Audience belief that the author is reliable (accurate 90% of the time)
  // rather than a hack (accurate 30%). Below the line, readers mostly stop
  // paying attention, so new work is rarely noticed.
  let logOdds = 3;                      // starts as a respected scholar
  return range(60).map(t => {
    const care = t >= lapseStart && t < lapseStart + lapseLength ? 0.3 : 0.9;
    const good = r() < care;
    const p = 1 / (1 + Math.exp(-logOdds));
    const noticed = p >= line || r() < 0.15;
    if (noticed) logOdds += good ? Math.log(0.9 / 0.3) : Math.log(0.1 / 0.7);
    logOdds = Math.max(-12, Math.min(12, logOdds));
    return {t: t + 1, trust: 1 / (1 + Math.exp(-logOdds)), care, good, noticed};
  });
}
```

## R {.unlisted}

```{.r}
# The John Yoo Line: once trust is lost, careful work goes unnoticed.
lapse_start <- 15 # when the author gets careless (piece #) # <1>
lapse_length <- 12 # how long the lapse lasts
line <- 0.5 # trust threshold (the line)
set.seed(41) # <2>

# Belief that the author is reliable (right 90% of the time) rather than a
# hack (30%). Below the line, readers mostly stop paying attention.
log_odds <- 3
trust <- numeric(60)
for (t in 1:60) {
  careless <- t > lapse_start & t <= lapse_start + lapse_length
  good <- runif(1) < if (careless) 0.3 else 0.9 # <3>
  noticed <- plogis(log_odds) >= line || runif(1) < 0.15 # <4>
  if (noticed) {
    log_odds <- log_odds + if (good) log(0.9 / 0.3) else log(0.1 / 0.7) # <5>
  }
  log_odds <- min(12, max(-12, log_odds))
  trust[t] <- plogis(log_odds)
}
below <- which(trust < line)
if (length(below)) {
  cat("Trust falls below the line at piece ", below[1], "\n", sep = "")
  back <- which(trust >= line & seq_along(trust) > below[1])
  cat(if (length(back)) {
    paste("Back above the line at piece", back[1])
  } else {
    "Trust never recovers within 60 pieces"
  }, "\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("Trust never falls below the line\n")
}

plot(1:60, trust, # <6>
  type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#2166ac", ylim = c(0, 1),
  xlab = "Piece", ylab = "Audience trust"
)
rect(lapse_start + 0.5, -1, lapse_start + lapse_length + 0.5, 2,
  col = adjustcolor("#d6604d", 0.1), border = NA
)
abline(h = line, lty = 2)
```
1. The page's controls: when the author's careless stretch starts, how long it lasts, and where the trust threshold sits.
2. Fixes the random numbers so the run is reproducible.
3. Each piece is good with high probability, except during the careless stretch.
4. Readers notice a piece only while they still trust the author, or by chance.
5. A noticed piece updates the readers' belief that the author is reliable.
6. Trust over 60 pieces. Once it falls below the line, careful work goes unread and trust rarely recovers.

## Python {.unlisted}

```{.python}
# The John Yoo Line: once trust is lost, careful work goes unnoticed.
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

lapse_start = 15   # when the author gets careless (piece #)
lapse_length = 12  # how long the lapse lasts
line = 0.5         # trust threshold (the line)
rng = np.random.default_rng(47)

# Belief that the author is reliable (right 90% of the time) rather than a
# hack (30%). Below the line, readers mostly stop paying attention.
log_odds = 3
trust = []
for t in range(1, 61):
    careless = lapse_start < t <= lapse_start + lapse_length
    good = rng.uniform() < (0.3 if careless else 0.9)
    noticed = 1 / (1 + np.exp(-log_odds)) >= line or rng.uniform() < 0.15
    if noticed:
        log_odds += np.log(0.9 / 0.3) if good else np.log(0.1 / 0.7)
    log_odds = min(12, max(-12, log_odds))
    trust.append(1 / (1 + np.exp(-log_odds)))
trust = np.array(trust)
pieces = np.arange(1, 61)
below = pieces[trust < line]
if below.size:
    print(f"Trust falls below the line at piece {below[0]}")
    back = pieces[(trust >= line) & (pieces > below[0])]
    print(f"Back above the line at piece {back[0]}" if back.size
          else "Trust never recovers within 60 pieces")
else:
    print("Trust never falls below the line")

plt.axvspan(lapse_start + 0.5, lapse_start + lapse_length + 0.5,
            color="#d6604d", alpha=0.1)
plt.plot(pieces, trust, color="#2166ac", linewidth=2)
plt.axhline(line, color="black", linestyle="--")
plt.ylim(0, 1)
plt.xlabel("Piece")
plt.ylabel("Audience trust")
plt.show()
```

## Key takeaways

::: takeaways
- Reputation creates the incentive for careful work. When it's lost, so is the incentive.
- Credibility is slow to rebuild once enough evidence of error has accumulated.
- Readers should update on track records and not assume every credentialed author is trying to be accurate.
:::
